content.value_statement: Teams need commit messages that are consistent, reviewable, and linked to issues. This skill formats changes using Sentry conventions, conventional types, and clear footers.
actual_capabilities: Defines the required commit header structure with optional scope.
Lists Sentry commit types and explains when to use each one.
Guides subject lines with imperative tense and length limits.
Helps add Fixes and Refs footers for GitHub, Sentry, and Linear issues.
Provides examples for fixes, features, refactors, breaking changes, and reverts.
limitations: Does not inspect Git diffs or run Git commands.
Does not validate issue keys against external systems.
Does not enforce repository policy outside the provided conventions.
Focuses on Sentry commit style, not every conventional commit variant.

use_cases.title: Standardize team commits
use_cases.description: Create consistent commit messages for feature work, fixes, documentation, tests, and maintenance changes.

use_cases.title: Improve review history
use_cases.description: Rewrite unclear draft messages into concise headers, useful bodies, and accurate issue footers.

use_cases.title: Prepare release traces
use_cases.description: Use Fixes and Refs footers so merged commits connect cleanly to issue trackers.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic message
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a short change description.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Sentry-style commit message for this change: [describe change]. Use the correct type and include a footer if needed.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite a draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this draft commit message to follow Sentry conventions: [draft]. Keep lines short and explain what and why.

prompt_templates.title: Add issue references
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a message that links work to issue trackers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Sentry-style commit message for [change summary]. Include the correct Fixes or Refs footer for [issue key].

prompt_templates.title: Handle complex changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for breaking changes or reverts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose a Sentry-style commit message for [change summary]. Include scope, body, footer, and breaking-change or revert wording if appropriate.

output_examples.input: A bug fix prevents deleted users from crashing the dashboard and closes SENTRY-5678.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a fix message with an api scope, a concise subject, a body explaining the null response, and a SENTRY footer.

output_examples.input: A feature adds Slack thread replies for alert updates and references GH-1234.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a feature message with an alerts scope, motivation in the body, and a GitHub reference footer.

output_examples.input: A revert removes a change that caused a production performance regression.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a revert message that names the original change and states the regression reason clearly.

best_practices: Provide a concise change summary before asking for a commit message.
Include issue keys when the commit should close or reference work.
Ask for a rewrite when an existing commit message is too long or unclear.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to invent issue keys or release details.
Do not mix unrelated changes into one commit message.
Do not use it as a replacement for project-specific policy review.

faq.question: What commit format does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses Sentry-style conventional commit messages with type, optional scope, subject, body, and footer guidance.

faq.question: Does this skill run Git commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides writing guidance and examples. It does not inspect diffs or execute commands.

faq.question: Can it handle breaking changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for breaking-change markers and footer text.

faq.question: Can it reference issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports Fixes and Refs patterns for Sentry, GitHub, and Linear issue identifiers.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it only useful for Sentry repositories?
faq.answer: It is best for Sentry-style repositories, but many conventions align with general conventional commits.
